messages:
eva: Nightly eval alert for v13c landed an hour ago — conv-sqa promptset failure rate jumped from 5% -> 38%. Not a single aligned answer in the top 10 for several seeds. :alarm:

sam: Copy. Do we have a failing diff that points to tokenization or model weights?

maya: Putting artifact link: https://artifacts.redwood/internal/nightly/2026-03-18/v13c/conv-sqa.tar.gz (has examples + generation traces). Quick peek shows repeated odd token splitting on contractions.

nate: Reproducer run on local with same checkpoint. I can repro generative inconsistency when `--kv-prefetch=true` (runtime flag). With prefetch off it's closer to baseline. Sharing command/logs:

```
# repro
rd-infer --model v13c --prompt-file conv-sqa.samples --batch-size 2 --kv-prefetch=true --seed 42
...
Generation 27: "I can ' t ..." -> tokens: ["I", "can", "\u2019", "t"]
```

liam: That's interesting — there was a small tokenizer normalization tweak in the v13c tokenizer patch: unicode apostrophe normalization + updated merges. Could interact with KV indexing.

eva: @liam did that change also shift token IDs for common contractions? Even a 1-2 token offset could cascade in cached KV retrieval.

liam: Yes, some merges changed. We tried to keep token ID mapping stable but shuffles in the tail happened. I can post the mapping diff.

maya: Example failure from artifact (prompt id 1042):

```
Prompt: "What's the capital of New Zealand?"
v13b response: "Wellington." (correct)
v13c response: "Welling ton." -> model then attempts to continue and hallucinates: "Welling ton is the largest city..."
```

sam: Looks like token break introduced a space mid-token which leads to KV cache keys differing. That would explain divergence after first few tokens.

nate: Quick experiment: toggling `--prefill-kv=false` during streaming reduces failure rate in batch runs by ~70%. Suggests prefill/prefetch path bug.

ops-bot: Deploy note: v13c rolled to stable at 2026-03-18T02:12Z via canary -> full. Canary logs show no errors.

eva: Can we do an emergency mitigation? Options: roll back tokenizer-only change for v13c, disable kv-prefetch default in serving, or patch compatibility mapping (slow). Which is fastest?

liam: Short term: flip default `kv-prefetch` to false in hosted runway for v13c only. I'll open a quick diff. Medium term: compute a token-id compatibility map and add a compat layer in runtime to translate KV keys during warmup.

sam: Agree. Also need to run the nightly eval across other promptsets (chat-inform, long-context) to check broader impact. I can queue that.

maya: I'll tag a set of representative prompts and run per-prompt diffs, pushing to the regression dashboard. If we hit more than 3 sets with >10% drop we trigger rollback.

eva: Nate, can you craft a minimal unit test that reproduces the KV misalignment so eng-runtime can triage quickly? Put it in `eng-runtime/tests/kv_token_compat_test.py` and link here.

nate: On it. Draft test uses the broken tokenizer pairs and toggles prefill. Will push in ~30m.

eval-bot: Nightly job summary: v13b -> v13c diff: conv-sqa -33% exact match, chat-inform -4%, long-context +1%. Full logs -> https://evals.redwood/internal/compare/v13b_v13c/2026-03-18

sam: Good catch by nightly. Let's prioritize the quick default flip + regression sweep. I'll coordinate roll and notify SRE.

eva: Thanks all. Keep this thread updated with the rollback toggle timestamp and test PR link. :thumbsup:
